SET @Image 1 as Marcus Vance — approved character reference sheet. Lock his exact facial identity, Black skin tone, muscular build, short tightly curled black hair, trimmed beard, navy-blue maintenance coveralls, yellow reflective bands, utility belt, heavy work boots, and RIGHT-hand flashlight.

SET @Image 2 as Level -99 Endless Hotel Corridor — approved environment reference sheet. Lock the aged beige wallpaper, dark wooden hotel doors, geometric brown-and-orange carpet, warm wall sconces, yellow-white fluorescent ceiling lights, and impossible corridor geometry.

SET @Image 3 as Buster — approved TMS-CHAR-BUSTER-001 character reference sheet. Lock the small golden-retriever-mix puppy's golden-tan fur, darker floppy ears, cream chest, dark brown eyes, black nose, and natural puppy proportions.

SET @Image 5 as Level -99 Shifting Door — approved TMS-ENV-SHIFTING-DOOR-001 environment reference sheet. Lock the aged dark wooden door, worn frame, tarnished handle, and short vertical black electrical-tape marker on its frame.

SET @Image 6 as EP04 Part 2 Starting Frame — approved TMS-EP04-P2-START-001. Use this image as the EXACT OPENING COMPOSITION for Part 2. Camera positioned inside the apparent alternate corridor, looking outward through the open dark wooden doorway toward Marcus and Buster. Both characters are completely outside the threshold, with Marcus holding his flashlight in his RIGHT hand and Buster beside his LEFT boot. Preserve camera perspective, doorway orientation, lighting, character blocking, costume, and environment.

DY,

THE MIDNIGHT SHIFT — EP04: THE FALSE EXIT
PART 2 OF 2 — UPDATED WITH @Image 6

Subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is Marcus Vance, referenced by @Image 1 and positioned according to @Image 6 — a muscular 32-year-old Black male maintenance worker with short tightly curled black hair, a neatly trimmed beard, dark brown eyes, navy-blue maintenance coveralls with yellow reflective bands, heavy work boots, and a utility belt containing a wrench, rope, and black electrical tape. His heavy-duty flashlight ALWAYS remains in his RIGHT hand. His LEFT hand remains available for physical interactions.

<Subject 2> is the Level -99 Endless Hotel Corridor, referenced by @Image 2 — an impossible windowless 1980s–1990s hotel hallway with aged beige wallpaper, repeating dark wooden doors, geometric brown-and-orange carpet, warm wall sconces, dark wooden baseboards, and yellow-white fluorescent ceiling fixtures. Its architecture may connect to itself through impossible spatial loops, but all visible physical interactions must remain realistic.

<Subject 3> is Buster, referenced by @Image 3 and positioned according to @Image 6 — a small golden-retriever-mix puppy with golden-tan fur, darker floppy ears, cream-colored chest, dark brown eyes, black nose, and no collar. Preserve his approved appearance and proportions. He remains close to Marcus's LEFT leg.

<Subject 4> is the Open Unmarked Hotel Door, referenced by @Image 6 for its opening composition and by @Image 2 for its architectural design — an aged dark wooden hotel door on the RIGHT wall of the original corridor, with a tarnished metal handle and worn hinges. It has no electrical-tape marker. At the beginning of Part 2, it is fully OPEN and stationary. Marcus and Buster are outside it in the original corridor.

<Subject 5> is the Wallpaper Navigation Marker — a short vertical strip of matte black electrical tape attached at chest height to the stained beige wallpaper in the original corridor. Marcus placed this marker during Part 1. It is NOT attached to any doorframe.

<Subject 6> is the Marked Shifting Door, referenced by @Image 5 — the previously encountered dark wooden hotel door with a separate short vertical black electrical-tape marker attached to its wooden frame beside the handle. Preserve the approved door and tape-marker appearance established in EP03.

Roles:

<Subject 1>: Protagonist investigating a possible escape route.
<Subject 2>: Primary environment and impossible spatial loop.
<Subject 3>: Companion and early-warning animal.
<Subject 4>: Open doorway leading into the apparent alternate corridor.
<Subject 5>: Fixed navigation marker proving the route has looped.
<Subject 6>: Previously marked shifting door confirming the return to the same area.

Reference_mapping:

@Image 1 → <Subject 1>: Marcus's exact facial identity, clothing, and equipment.

@Image 2 → <Subject 2>: Corridor architecture, materials, and lighting.

@Image 3 → <Subject 3>: Buster's exact approved appearance.

@Image 5 → <Subject 6>: Marked shifting door and vertical tape marker.

@Image 6 → <Subject 1>, <Subject 3>, <Subject 4>: Starting-frame composition, character blocking, open-door orientation, and camera position.

@Image 2 + @Image 6 → <Subject 4>: Doorway materials and spatial layout.

@Image 5 → <Subject 5>: Black electrical-tape material only; the wallpaper marker is a separate physical object.

@Image 4: Previously approved vending-machine reference, not visible in this Part.

REFERENCE PRIORITY:

Character identity: @Image 1 and @Image 3.
Environment architecture: @Image 2.
Marked shifting-door appearance: @Image 5.
Opening composition and blocking: @Image 6.

If visual details conflict, preserve the approved character identity from @Image 1 and @Image 3, while using @Image 6 for camera angle, doorway position, and starting poses.

Do not treat @Image 6 as a new character design.

IMPORTANT:
<Subject 4> is the UNMARKED open door.
<Subject 5> is the tape marker on WALLPAPER.
<Subject 6> is the previously marked door with tape on its WOODEN FRAME.

These are separate physical elements.

summary:

Marcus and Buster stand outside an open hotel door revealing what appears to be a different corridor.

They cautiously pass through the doorway.

Marcus explores the hallway with Buster.

Buster suddenly stops.

Marcus discovers the same black electrical-tape marker he placed on the wallpaper moments earlier.

The previously marked shifting door is also visible farther along the LEFT wall.

Marcus realizes that the apparent escape route has returned them to the same corridor.

The door they used closes behind them.

The episode ends with an unexplained handle rattle from the other side.

Narrative:
Apparent Escape → Exploration → Recognition → Trap Revealed.

Starting_frame_lock:

Use @Image 6 as the exact opening visual reference.

At local 00:00.000:

- Camera is positioned INSIDE the apparent alternate corridor.
- Camera faces outward through the OPEN doorway.
- Marcus stands completely OUTSIDE the doorway.
- Both of Marcus's boots remain on the original corridor carpet.
- Buster stands beside Marcus's LEFT boot.
- Marcus's flashlight is held in his RIGHT hand.
- The flashlight points into the doorway.
- The dark wooden door is fully OPEN.
- The door is stationary.
- The threshold is clearly visible.
- No character has crossed the threshold.
- Preserve the camera axis and doorway orientation of @Image 6.
- Do not reposition Marcus or Buster inside the room before the walking action begins.

Cross-Part continuity:

Part 1 ends with Marcus and Buster outside the open doorway.

Part 2 begins with the same blocking and prop state.

Part 1 camera: original corridor side.
Part 2 camera: reverse angle from inside the apparent alternate corridor.

This is a deliberate HARD CUT.

No frame-perfect camera movement is required between Parts.

<Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, <Subject 3>, and <Subject 4> visible. Opening composition follows @Image 6. Marcus and Buster cross the doorway.

detailed_description:

[Shot 1] At 00:00.000–00:03.500,

MEDIUM-WIDE SHOT, REVERSE CAMERA ANGLE, STATIC CAMERA.

START DIRECTLY FROM @Image 6.

The camera is positioned inside the apparent alternate hotel corridor, looking outward through the fully open dark wooden doorway.

Marcus stands beyond the doorway in the original corridor.

His identity and costume match @Image 1.

Buster stands beside his LEFT boot, matching @Image 3.

The open doorway, camera perspective, lighting, and character blocking match @Image 6.

Marcus holds his heavy-duty flashlight in his RIGHT hand.

He cautiously steps forward through the doorway.

His LEFT foot crosses the threshold first, followed by his RIGHT foot.

Buster follows him through the same opening.

Both fully enter the apparent alternate corridor.

The camera remains stationary.

The door stays OPEN behind them.

Do not begin with Marcus already inside.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.500–00:07.000,

MEDIUM REAR TRACKING SHOT, CAMERA FOLLOWING FROM BEHIND.

Marcus walks slowly along the apparently different corridor.

Buster trots beside his LEFT leg.

The camera follows from behind.

Marcus's RIGHT-hand flashlight illuminates the geometric carpet ahead.

The wallpaper, doors, baseboards, and fluorescent fixtures match @Image 2.

Marcus passes a dark wooden door.

The corridor appears empty.

Buster suddenly slows and stops.

Marcus takes one additional step before noticing.

He stops and looks down toward Buster.

[Shot 3] At 00:07.000–00:11.500,

MEDIUM THREE-QUARTER SHOT, SLOW CONTROLLED PAN.

Buster stands still, staring toward the LEFT side of the corridor.

Marcus follows his gaze.

The camera pans to reveal a short vertical strip of black electrical tape attached to the beige WALLPAPER at chest height.

This is the same navigation marker Marcus placed during Part 1.

The marker is NOT attached to a doorframe.

Marcus approaches and illuminates it with his RIGHT-hand flashlight.

He recognizes its placement and orientation.

Farther down the LEFT wall, the previously marked shifting door is visible.

That door matches @Image 5.

It retains its own separate vertical black electrical-tape marker on the WOODEN FRAME beside the handle.

Both tape markers are distinct physical objects.

Marcus realizes the corridor has looped back to the same area.

Buster remains close to his LEFT leg.

[Shot 4] At 00:11.500–00:15.000,

MEDIUM SHOT, THREE-QUARTER FRONT ANGLE, STATIC CAMERA.

Marcus turns toward the doorway they entered through.

The same unmarked wooden door is visible behind him.

It is still OPEN at the beginning of the shot.

Marcus remains several steps away.

Buster stands beside his LEFT boot.

Without anyone touching it, the door begins slowly swinging toward its frame.

The camera remains on the corridor side.

The empty space beyond the doorway becomes progressively obscured.

The door closes completely with a heavy wooden impact.

Marcus and Buster remain OUTSIDE the closed door, in the corridor.

Marcus raises his RIGHT-hand flashlight toward the sealed doorway.

The handle rattles once from the other side.

No person or creature is visible.

Buster freezes.

CUT TO BLACK at exactly 00:15.000.

END PART 2.

Ending_state:

Marcus and Buster remain in the looping Level -99 corridor.

The unmarked doorway is closed.

The wallpaper navigation marker remains attached to the wall.

The marked shifting door remains farther along the LEFT wall.

Marcus's flashlight remains in his RIGHT hand.

No visible entity is revealed.

Visual_and_continuity_constraints:

- Opening composition must match @Image 6.
- Marcus's identity and costume must match @Image 1.
- Corridor architecture must match @Image 2.
- Buster's identity and appearance must match @Image 3.
- Marked shifting door must match @Image 5.
- Flashlight remains in Marcus's RIGHT hand throughout.
- Buster stays close to Marcus's LEFT leg.
- Marcus and Buster cross the threshold only during Shot 1.
- Both must be inside the alternate corridor before Shot 2.
- The open doorway remains behind them.
- The apparent alternate corridor loops back to the original area.
- The wallpaper marker and doorframe marker remain separate.
- Never duplicate or exchange tape markers.
- The unmarked door remains free of tape.
- The door closes realistically on its hinges.
- No character teleportation.
- No doors sliding through walls.
- No unauthorized humans or visible monsters.
- No red flashlight flicker.
- No dialogue, narration, or captions.
- No red blood or unnecessary weapons.
- No background music.

00:11.500–00:15.000:
Aged wooden door hinges creaking, heavy door-closing impact, one metallic handle rattle, Buster's startled breathing.

Cut to silence at 00:15.000.

Environmental ambience and synchronized diegetic SFX only.
No background music.
